prompt:
Build a physically causal closed-loop forced-air cooling system for a CPU board. The thermal plant must contain distinct finite thermal masses for the CPU, heat-sink base, and fins, joined by physical conductive heat-transfer paths. A physical fan, inlet and outlet gas path, heat-sink flow channel, and case-flow restriction must remove heat from the fins by forced convection. Measured CPU temperature must control the real fan power path; the controller form is not prescribed. Prescribing temperature traces, copying the target, or reporting airflow that is disconnected from the thermal plant is not valid.

Use a CPU temperature target of 50 degC. Read CPUHeatScale, AmbientTemperature_K, AirflowRestrictionScale, FanCapacityScale, and InitialTemperature_C from MATLAB base-workspace variables. Their nominal values are 1.0, 293.15 K, 1.0, 1.0, and 30 degC, and their supported ranges are 0.8--1.25, 288.15--308.15 K, 0.8--1.6, 0.8--1.1, and 25--45 degC. CPUHeatScale multiplies this heat-input schedule: 50 W initially, 35 W from 620 s, 10 W from 4000 s, 45 W from 7000 s, and 20 W from 8300 s. AirflowRestrictionScale must act on the physical gas-flow resistance, and FanCapacityScale must act on the physical fan capability.

Across the declared range, keep all temperatures, fan motion, gas flow, pressure rise, and heat flows finite. The controller must increase cooling effort when required, limit CPU temperature, and recover after changes in heat generation. Changes in ambient temperature, flow restriction, and fan capacity must causally affect the same physical cooling path.

Log complete-run MATLAB Timeseries named thermal_state, fan_state, and heat_flow. thermal_state has 4 channels in this order: CPU, heat-sink-base, and fin temperature followed by the 50 degC target, all in degC. fan_state has 3 channels in this order: physical fan speed (rpm), air mass flow (kg/s), and fan pressure rise (Pa). heat_flow has 4 channels in this order: physical CPU heat input, CPU-to-base conduction, base-to-fin conduction, and fin-to-air heat transfer, all in W. Save the completed model as cand_XTHERM07.slx in the submission directory and keep the latest usable state saved there throughout the task.

Submission filename contract: create, edit, and save the final self-contained Simulink model as cand_XTHERM07.slx in the assigned submission directory; keep the latest usable state at that exact path throughout the run.
